BUS.G12.T1.HR.A1.title: The Human Resources function
BUS.G12.T1.HR.A1.description: Relevant legislation and the aspects of the human resources function: recruitment and selection; employee contracts; induction and placement; salary administration (including personal tax); employee benefits; and skills development (the Skills Development Act, SETAs, learnerships, the NQF and SAQA).
BUS.G12.T1.HR.A1.strand: T1 — Legislation, Human Resources, ethics, creative thinking & business strategies
BUS.G12.T1.HR.A1.recovery_strategy: Recruitment attracts applicants, selection chooses, induction settles them in, and skills development grows them. Salary administration includes deducting personal tax (PAYE). SETAs and learnerships develop skills under the Skills Development Act.

questions.question: _________ is the process of attracting suitable applicants, while selection chooses the best of them.
questions.expected: Recruitment
questions.memo: Recruitment attracts applicants (e.g. by advertising); selection then chooses the most suitable one.

questions.question: What do induction and placement involve?
options: Settling a new employee in and assigning them to the right role
questions.expected: Settling a new employee in and assigning them to the right role
questions.memo: Induction settles the new employee into the workplace, and placement assigns them to the job that best fits them.

questions.question: True or false: Skills development includes learnerships and is supported by SETAs.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Skills development uses tools like learnerships, coordinated by SETAs under the Skills Development Act.

questions.question: Salary _________ covers paying staff and deducting tax correctly.
questions.expected: administration
questions.memo: Salary administration manages how staff are paid, including deductions such as personal income tax.

questions.question: Which of these is a deduction from an employee's salary that goes to the government?
questions.expected: Personal income tax (PAYE)
questions.memo: Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) is personal income tax deducted from an employee's salary and paid to the government.

questions.question: True or false: Pension and medical aid are examples of employee benefits.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Benefits such as pension and medical aid are rewards beyond the basic salary that help attract and keep staff.

questions.question: Put the stages of the HR employment cycle in a sensible order.

items.text: Induct and place the new employee

questions.expected: recruit, select, contract, induct
questions.memo: Attract applicants, choose the best, sign the contract, then induct and place the new employee.

questions.question: Sort each task into the HR activity it belongs to.

items.text: Sending workers on a SETA training course

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Interviewing and advertising = recruitment/selection; PAYE and net pay = salary administration; learnerships and SETA courses = skills development.

questions.question: What do the NQF and SAQA relate to?
options: A national framework that records and recognises qualifications
questions.expected: A national framework that records and recognises qualifications
questions.memo: The National Qualifications Framework (NQF) and the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA) organise and recognise qualifications.

questions.question: A structured programme that combines workplace experience with formal study is called a _________.
questions.expected: learnership
questions.memo: A learnership combines on-the-job experience with study, leading to a recognised qualification.

questions.question: Why is good induction of new employees important?
options: It helps them become productive sooner and reduces staff turnover
It increases the company's tax bill
It replaces the need for any training
It slows the new employee down on purpose
questions.expected: It helps them become productive sooner and reduces staff turnover
questions.memo: A good induction settles new staff quickly, so they reach productivity sooner and are more likely to stay.

questions.question: True or false: An employment contract should comply with the Basic Conditions of Employment Act.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Employment contracts must meet the minimum standards set by the BCEA, such as hours and leave.

questions.question: Sort each item into recruitment, selection or induction.

items.text: Giving the new hire a tour and a mentor
Explaining policies on the first day

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Adverts attract (recruit); interviews and tests choose (select); tours and policy briefings settle people in (induct).

questions.question: A worker is paid R50 for every chair they assemble, with no fixed monthly amount. How is this pay best described?
questions.expected: Piecemeal (per-unit) pay
questions.memo: Paying a set amount per item produced is piecemeal (piece-rate) pay, based on output rather than time.

questions.question: What is the role of a SETA?
options: To fund and coordinate skills training within an industry sector
To set the price of consumer goods
questions.expected: To fund and coordinate skills training within an industry sector
questions.memo: Sector Education and Training Authorities (SETAs) use the skills levy to fund and organise training in their sector.

questions.question: Personal income tax deducted directly from an employee's salary is commonly called _________.
questions.expected: PAYE
questions.memo: PAYE (Pay-As-You-Earn) is the personal income tax deducted from salaries and paid over to the tax authority.

questions.question: A business struggles to find skilled workers. Which HR action best addresses this in the long term?
options: Using learnerships and SETA training to develop its own skilled staff
questions.expected: Using learnerships and SETA training to develop its own skilled staff
questions.memo: Skills development through learnerships and SETA-funded training builds the skilled workforce the business needs over time.

questions.question: Why must an employer handle employee contracts and salaries within the relevant labour laws?
options: To stay compliant, treat staff fairly and avoid disputes or penalties
Because the laws have no effect on business
questions.expected: To stay compliant, treat staff fairly and avoid disputes or penalties
questions.memo: Following labour law on contracts and pay keeps the business compliant, protects employees and prevents costly disputes.

questions.question: How can a strong benefits package (pension, medical aid, leave) help a business?
options: It helps attract and retain good employees
It guarantees the business never pays tax
It removes the need to pay any salary
It lowers the quality of staff
questions.expected: It helps attract and retain good employees
questions.memo: Good benefits make a business more attractive to work for, helping it recruit and keep skilled staff.

questions.question: How do the HR activities and the relevant Acts fit together?
options: HR carries out recruitment, contracts, pay and development within the limits set by labour legislation
HR and the Acts are completely unrelated
The Acts apply only to marketing
HR can ignore the law when convenient
questions.expected: HR carries out recruitment, contracts, pay and development within the limits set by labour legislation
questions.memo: The HR function operates inside the framework of the BCEA, EEA, LRA, COIDA and SDA, which shape how staff are hired, paid, protected and developed.
